results.summary_before: This project implements a digital three-phase generator that produces three square-wave outputs with 120-degree phase shifts from a single input clock. It uses a 3-bit Johnson counter and provides both normal and complementary outputs. The design was simulated in Quartus II and tested on an Altera Cyclone II FPGA, but it requires external signal generation and an oscilloscope for verification. The intended application is to drive three-phase motors after analog filtering, although the chip only outputs digital signals.

results.summary_before: badGPU is a basic GPU that rasterizes up to four triangles at 640x480 60Hz with 6-bit color, controlled by a host microcontroller over SPI. It supports a programmable background color and uses polygon ordering instead of a Z-buffer, with vertices limited to 80 X and 60 Y positions. The design requires a Tiny VGA PMOD, a VGA screen, and an SPI-capable microcontroller, and it asserts an interrupt during blanking to accept new commands. It is notable for fitting a simple polygon rasterizer into a 4x2 tile Tiny Tapeout design.

results.summary_before: This design implements an <8,0> posit division circuit, accepting two 8-bit posit inputs via ui and uio and outputting the 8-bit quotient on uo. Pre-fabrication testing compared simulated outputs against a software-generated table for all possible input pairs, and post-fabrication testing requires supplying input posit values and observing the quotient on the output pins. External hardware such as a microcontroller or DIP switches is needed to drive the input pins. The design is notable for supporting the posit number format, an alternative to IEEE floating point.

results.summary_before: This project implements the classic game Pong on raw silicon, generating VGA video and stereo audio. It uses a custom VGA sync module and pixel-clock-based logic to render sprites and background colors. The game is controlled by six buttons for two players (up, down, serve for each). External hardware includes a TinyVGA Pmod and buttons with pull-down resistors.
